summary: The archive as object. A new Research-field entry archival_turn (period_4) gathers the readership that the History PhD citation graph identifies as the broadest post-2000 framework without an opposing side: the archive as a site of power (Trouillot, Mbembe, Schwartz and Cook), Stoler's reading along the grain and the Dutch reviewers' doubts, the archive's allure, fever and dust (Farge, Derrida, Steedman), absence and critical fabulation (Hartman, Fuentes), archive stories and the ethnography of archives (Burton, Dirks, Zeitlyn), and the archivists' turn in Canada and South Africa, in six strands, a roster of 16, a chronology of 27 events from 1989 to 2024, and seven field arrows (three more are held, include: false, after Sol's review). Ann Laura Stoler (promoted from a people record; 7 new edges, 15 events) and Michel-Rolph Trouillot (new; 8 edges, 24 events) become person entries in the historians layer. edge_386 and edge_417 are re-sourced from post to ann_laura_stoler; derrida_archive_primary loses its mirror-host URL.
rationale: Research of 2026-10-23: data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-archive.md (agent A: §0 project state and dissertation figures; §§1–13 readings with read status; P.1–P.10 proposals). Every edge rests on a read text in the author's own words or on a named reader's explicit statement, and the notes say which: Stoler's 2002 abstract; Along the Archival Grain through Gouda and Schulte Nordholt (read in full, page numbers given); Carnal Knowledge through Ottevaere; Imperial Debris through Schultz; Trouillot through Craipain (p. 98), Bulamah–Goyatá–Pereira and Davidson (unpaginated; wording awaits a library copy of Silencing the Past, ch. 1); Cook 2001 in part; Schwartz–Cook, Mbembe, Manoff, Zeitlyn by abstract. Dissertation figures (History PhD citation graph, release 2026-10-23) appear in scope notes and strand text only. After Sol's review (release/fixes-1.156-A.md): the New School appointment, the 1991 Savage Slot printing, the 1993 chair and the 2001 Current Anthropology date are no longer dated events; Trouillot 1995 is year precision; Daut 2021 stays not_checked.

edge_386.relationship: Race and the Education of Desire (1995) questioned the marginal place of race and empire in Foucault's history of sexuality while using his 1976 lectures; Carnal Knowledge asked 'why Foucault's elusive and suggestive treatment of race still remains so marginal to what colonial historians take from him today' (2002, p. 141, as quoted by Ottevaere)
edge_386.evidence_note: Period-4 wave 1 (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-archive.md P.9 2) re-sourced this arrow from post to the new person entry ann_laura_stoler, keeping its id and kind, because its claim was hers alone. Earlier note retained: the checked publisher description of Race and the Education of Desire (1995) records a critique of the marginal place of empire, and of race in the making of bourgeois sexuality, in Foucault alongside productive use of his 1976 lectures and Dutch and French colonial archives; the book itself is unread; Spivak's critique of Foucault is the separate edge from her person entry. Added: Ottevaere 2004 (read in full), quoting Carnal Knowledge, p. 141 ('why Foucault's elusive and suggestive treatment of race still remains so marginal'), and ch. 6, 'A Colonial Reading of Foucault' (UC Press contents); Schultz 2015 (read): 'First it was Michel Foucault's Collège de France lectures about the biopolitics of race'.

edge_417.relationship: Sexuality and racial formation investigated through colonial archives: 'the micromanagement of sexual arrangements … was critical to the distinctions between ruler and ruled' (1995, as quoted by Gouda); 'sexual control was both an instrumental image for the body politic … and itself fundamental to how racial policies were secured' (2002, p. 78, as quoted by Ottevaere)
edge_417.evidence_note: Period-4 wave 1 (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-archive.md P.9 2) re-sourced this arrow from post to the new person entry ann_laura_stoler, keeping its id and kind. Earlier note retained: the 1995 project both uses and questions Foucault; this contribution is the specific colonial-historical intervention described by the publisher, not the origin of queer history or proof that all queer historians adopted it. Added: Gouda 2009, p. 553 (read in full), quoting the 1995 book without a page; Ottevaere 2004 (read in full), quoting Carnal Knowledge, p. 78.

text_revisions.new: Reworks Foucault through colonial archives, race and sexuality (1995); treats 'colonizer/colonized' as 'a historically shifting pair of social categories that needs to be explained' (2002, p. 13, as quoted by Ottevaere); asks scholars to move 'from archive-as-source to archive-as-subject' (2002).
